notes: Taken from the Board of Elections' 46-day election notice, which lists every contest and issue with the precincts that vote on it, with candidates' parties from the Board's candidate list and issue details from its certified questions and issues list and individual notices of election. Long charter amendments are condensed; the full wording is on the sample ballot and in the full-text documents on the Board's 2026 page.

Candidates are listed alphabetically by last name, not in ballot order: Ohio rotates the order of names from precinct to precinct. Certified write-in candidates are not printed on the ballot and are not listed.

"Where you live" uses the state voter file: a district or school levy is shown for a city, village or township when any of its voters live in that district. Your exact ballot depends on your precinct.
Franklin County's voter file has no school districts, so school and library issues are placed using the precincts the Board's 46-day notice lists for each issue.

issues.text: Shall the Bexley City School District be authorized to do both of the following: 1. issues.title: Charter amendment (by petition): council members elected only by voters in their district
issues.text: This proposed charter amendment would limit the ability to vote for candidates for Columbus City Council to only those electors living within the districts that those candidates seek to represent. Ballots within council districts would include both citywide races and the district race, and a recall election of a district council member could be started by a petition signed by district electors equal to at least 15% of the votes cast in the district in the preceding mayoral election. Shall the proposed charter amendment be approved?

issues.title: Charter amendment (by Council): district-only voting for district seats, at-large seats added, 13-member Council
issues.text: This proposed charter amendment would limit the ability to vote for candidates for Columbus City Council to only those electors living within the districts that those candidates seek to represent. It adds two at-large council members elected in 2027 and two more elected in 2029 (four-year terms), moving from a nine-member to an eleven- and then a thirteen-member Council; redraws the council district map in 2027 and raises the allowed population variance between districts from 1% to 7.5%; requires district candidates to have lived in their district for a year before the primary; updates expulsion, quorum and vote requirements; sets petition signature requirements (150 district / 250 at-large); and allows recall of district and at-large members by petition. Shall the proposed charter amendment be approved?

issues.title: Charter amendment: RES-0026 (mayoral primary)
issues.text: Shall Section 3.01, Election and Term, of Article III, Mayor, be amended to eliminate the mayoral primary election when no more than two candidates have filed for the office of Mayor?

issues.title: Charter amendment: RES-0027 (qualifications of elected officials)
issues.text: Shall Section 3.02, Qualifications, of Article III, Mayor; Section 4.03, Qualifications, of Article IV, The Council; and Section 10.02, Qualifications, of Article X, Department of Law, be amended to establish a consistent standard regarding conflicts with other public offices and public employment for the Mayor, Council Members and the City Attorney?

issues.title: Charter amendment: RES-0028 (ward boundary adjustment)
issues.text: Shall Section 4.02, Composition and Term, of Article IV, The Council, be amended to revise the process for adjusting ward boundaries to base it on federal decennial census population data and specified population disparity criteria?

issues.title: Charter amendment: RES-0029 (legislative procedure: council abstentions)
issues.text: Shall Section 4.12, Legislative Procedure, of Article IV, The Council, be amended to require that an alleged improper voting abstention by a Council member be subject to the notice and hearing procedures for removal established in the Charter?

issues.title: Charter amendment: RES-0030 (administrative departments)
issues.text: Shall Article V, Administrative Departments, be amended to remove department listings, preserving the Charter duties of the Director of Finance, and making related organizational changes?

issues.title: Charter amendment: RES-0031 (City Attorney)
issues.text: Shall Sections 10.01, City Attorney, and 10.03, General Powers and Duties, of Article X, Department of Law, be amended to clarify the process for filling vacancies in the office of the City Attorney, update the powers and duties of the office, and make related grammatical revisions?

issues.title: Charter amendment: RES-0032 (Planning Commission attendance)
issues.text: Shall Section 11.02, Planning Commission - Organization, of Article XI, Planning Commission, be amended to authorize the Planning Commission to establish attendance requirements for its members through its rules of operation?

issues.title: Charter amendment: RES-0033 (zoning appeals)
issues.text: Shall Section 11.03, Planning Commission - Powers and Duties, of Article XI, Planning Commission, be amended and Article XII, Board of Zoning and Building Appeals, be repealed to transfer zoning, building, and landscaping appeal functions to the Planning Commission and to transfer Planning Commission appeals to Franklin County courts?

issues.title: Charter amendment: RES-0034 (Charter Review Commission every ten years)
issues.text: Shall Section 22.01, Composition and Term, of Article XXII, Charter Review Commission, be amended to require that the Charter Review Commission be convened every ten years instead of every five years?

issues.title: Charter amendment: RES-0035 (non-discrimination)
issues.text: Shall Section 23.07, Non Discrimination Clause, of Article XXIII, General Provisions, be amended to update the Charter's nondiscrimination provisions to align with the City's Codified Ordinances and applicable federal, state, and local law?

issues.title: Charter amendment (by petition): Community Consent Amendment (referendum on large developments)
issues.text: Amends the city charter to include a new article, Article XI, to establish a mandatory public referendum process as a condition of approval for any proposed development, qualifiable business expansion, or transfer of property ownership that occupies 50 or more contiguous acres, draws or is designed to draw more than 20 megawatts of electrical power at peak capacity, or consumes or is projected to consume more than 500,000 gallons of water per day; and establishes enforceable community impact standards for any approved facility. Shall the charter amendment, as proposed by initiative, be adopted?

issues.text: Shall the Charter of the City of Worthington be amended to add Section 1.05 to read as follows: SECTION 1.05 REFERENDUM PETITION SIGNATURE REQUIREMENT. Notwithstanding any other provisions of this Charter, the power of referendum on any ordinance or other measure passed by the Council may be exercised in the manner provided by the laws of the State of Ohio except that the petition signature requirement shall be ten percent of the electors of the City, based on the total vote cast at the last preceding general municipal election?
